successCriteria: The mechanism is SN1. The slow first step is the C-Br bond breaking on its own to form a planar carbocation and Br-, and hydroxide plays no part in that step, so the rate depends only on the halogenoalkane: rate = k[(CH3)3CBr]. Hydroxide attacks the carbocation in a second, fast step.

Hydroxide attacks opposite the C-Br bond so its lone pair can form the new C-O bond as the C-Br pair leaves with bromine, through a single transition state. The rate equation, rate = k[CH3Br][OH-], includes both reactants, which shows both meet in the one slow step.
objectives.text: Explain electrophilic addition to ethene and the SN1 and SN2 substitution mechanisms, including their rate equations

successCriteria: Step 1: ethene + HBr gives bromoethane by electrophilic addition. Step 2: bromoethane + aqueous NaOH, heated, gives ethanol by nucleophilic substitution. Step 3: ethanol is partially oxidised with acidified K2Cr2O7 and heat, stopping at ethanal, CH3CHO, before further oxidation to ethanoic acid.
Curly arrows follow the electrons: they start at an electron-rich region (a lone pair or pi bond) and point to where the electrons go.
